step.detail:
Question: For clinical negligence claims in Northern Ireland, what does this page say about when legal aid is available, for adults, and any key limits or tests? Quote the exact wording.
The page says legal aid for a clinical negligence claim is applied for through "representation higher," and that the certificate is generally limited in stages rather than given as a full certificate at the outset. It does not mention any special rule for adults or any means/merits test on this page. The key limit described is that the certificate is often initially restricted to investigation and pre-action steps, then later to issuing proceedings and steps up to discovery, with further limitation or a full certificate sought by amendment request.
✓ quote found in the page: "You will need to make an application to representation higher."
✓ quote found in the page: "Generally, the Agency will limit the certificate to certain steps in proceedings so as to minimise the exposure of the fund in the early stages of the case."
✓ quote found in the page: "Often certificates will initially be limited to investigation of the potential claim under the pre-action protocol, including obtaining the assisted person’s medical records and consideration thereof."
✓ quote found in the page: "As the matter progresses, the next limitation is likely to be the issuing of proceedings, replies and steps up to obtaining discovery."

Question: What does this page say about the current complaints procedure, especially when it started and any documents setting standards or response times? Quote the exact wording.
The page says the current procedure starts “From 1 January 2026,” when all HSC organisations must follow the new model complaints handling procedure. It also says the new procedure “replaces the Department of Health’s previous Guidance and Directions on the HSC Complaints Procedure,” and the documents section lists “Guidance in relation to the Health and Social Care Complaints Procedure - April 2023.” The page states the response times as “usually within 5 working days” for Stage One and “within 20 working days” for Stage Two.
✓ quote found in the page: "From 1 January 2026, all Health and Social Care (HSC) organisations must follow the Northern Ireland Public Services Ombudsman Model Complaints Handling Procedure (MCHP)."
✓ quote found in the page: "From that date, the HSC MCHP replaces the Department of Health’s previous Guidance and Directions on the HSC Complaints Procedure."
✓ quote found in the page: "Stage One: Frontline response. This stage focuses on early resolution, usually within 5 working days, and as close as possible to the point where the service was provided."
✓ quote found in the page: "Stage Two: Full investigation. This stage takes a closer look at what happened and aims to provide a full response within 20 working days."

steps.what: Royal Victoria Hospital is part of Belfast Health and Social Care Trust, so complaints about the Emergency Department go first to Belfast Trust. Belfast Trust’s current page says you should usually complain within 6 months of the event, while the Northern Ireland public guidance says usually within 6 months of becoming aware of the cause for complaint and normally no longer than 12 months after the event; from 1 January 2026 the national HSC model procedure uses a 5-working-day Stage One frontline response and a 20-working-day Stage Two full investigation.

You can complain by email, phone, letter or the Trust’s online feedback form.
The Trust says: "We would usually ask that you do this within 6 months of the event taking place."
National public guidance says complaints should usually be within 6 months of becoming aware of the cause for complaint and normally no longer than 12 months after the event.
From 1 January 2026 all HSC organisations must follow the NIPSO Model Complaints Handling Procedure.
steps.appliesIf: Public Health and Social Care treatment at Royal Victoria Hospital, which is run by Belfast Health and Social Care Trust.
alternatives: You can also complain by email to complaints@belfasttrust.hscni.net, by phone on 028 9504 8000, or by letter to the Trust.

step.detail:
Question: What exact time limit does this legislation set for personal injury negligence claims in Northern Ireland, and how does the date of knowledge work? Quote the exact wording.
The legislation sets a time limit of three years for personal injury negligence claims: “that period is three years from— (a) the date on which the cause of action accrued, or (b) the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.” The date of knowledge is when the person first had knowledge that the injury was significant, attributable to the negligence, nuisance or breach of duty, and of the defendant’s identity (and, if relevant, the other person’s identity and supporting facts).

step.detail:
Question: What does this official explanatory note say about personal injury claims and any cap on the percentage of damages that may be taken as a success fee? Quote the exact wording.
The note says that article 4 specifies personal injury claims, and that in a claim for personal injuries the success fee is capped at 25% of specified damages. It also says this cap applies only at first instance; for appeals, the maximum success fee is 100% of those damages.
✓ quote found in the page: "Article 4 specifies claims for personal injury for these purposes."
✓ quote found in the page: "Article 5 provides that, in a claim for personal injuries, the success fee shall be limited to a maximum of 25% of the damages awarded for pain, suffering and loss of amenity and pecuniary loss, other than future pecuniary loss and net of any sums recoverable by the Compensation Recovery Unit, inclusive of VAT."
✓ quote found in the page: "Article 5 further limits the effect of the 25% cap to proceedings at first instance."
✓ quote found in the page: "In respect of all other personal injury proceedings (i.e. appeals), the maximum success fee which may be recovered from damages awarded for pain, suffering and loss of amenity and pecuniary loss, other than future pecuniary loss and net of any sums recoverable by the Compensation Recovery Unit, shall be a maximum of 100% of those damages, inclusive of VAT."

Question: What does this official page say about financial eligibility for legal aid advice and assistance in Northern Ireland? Quote the exact wording that matters.
The page says that to qualify financially for advice and assistance, the applicant’s capital and income must be within the current financial limits, and disposable income must be less than £234.00 per week. It also says a contribution is payable when disposable income is between £107 and £234 per week. The page further states that if disposable capital exceeds the set limit, the applicant is not eligible.
✓ quote found in the page: ""In order to qualify financially for advice and assistance the applicant’s capital and income must be within the current financial limits set out in Regulation 6 of the Financial Regulations.""
✓ quote found in the page: ""What is left after making these deductions is disposable income. To qualify for advice and assistance disposable income must be less than £234.00 per week.""
✓ quote found in the page: ""A contribution is payable when an applicant’s disposable income is between £107 and £234 per week.""
✓ quote found in the page: ""A client whose disposable capital exceeds the appropriate amount set out above is not eligible for advice and assistance (even if the client is in receipt of a passport benefit).""

Question: What does this official page say about the Clinical Negligence Team and the kinds of cases it handles for HSC bodies? Quote the exact wording.
The page says the Clinical Negligence Team is "the sole provider of advice, representation and training to the Public Health and Social Care sector in Northern Ireland" and that it handles "clinical negligence litigation and inquests" for its clients, including HSC Trusts. It says the team deals with negligence and loss allegations in "every area of clinical specialism" and gives examples such as birth injury, misdiagnosis, surgery delays, surgical complications, failure to refer, and failure to obtain informed consent.
✓ quote found in the page: "The Clinical Negligence (CN) Team of the Directorate of Legal Services (DLS) is the sole provider of advice, representation and training to the Public Health and Social Care sector in Northern Ireland."
✓ quote found in the page: "...deliver a comprehensive, high quality and cost-effective legal service to our valued clients in relation to clinical negligence litigation and inquests."
✓ quote found in the page: "This team works closely with the Trusts’ Litigation partners, carrying out extensive investigations into allegations of negligence and loss relating to every area of clinical specialism."
✓ quote found in the page: "Examples of the types of cases dealt with include birth injury, misdiagnosis or delay in diagnosis, surgery delays, surgical complications, failure to refer to appropriate specialist, failure to obtain informed consent."

steps.body: Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
steps.what: Royal Victoria Hospital is part of Belfast Health and Social Care Trust, so a complaint about the Emergency Department starts with Belfast Trust. The Trust’s current page says complaints should normally be made within six months of the event or of finding out there is a reason to complain, and its two-stage complaints handling procedure aims for a Stage 1 decision within 5 working days and a Stage 2 written response within 20 working days.

The Trust says its complaints handling procedure has two stages.

says.detail:
Legal aid FAQs - clinical negligence claims | Department of Justice (https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/legal-aid-faqs-clinical-negligence-claims)
The page says legal aid for a clinical negligence claim is applied for through "representation higher," and that the certificate is generally limited in stages rather than given as a full certificate at the outset. It does not mention any special rule for adults or any means/merits test on this page. The key limit described is that the certificate is often initially restricted to investigation and pre-action steps, then later to issuing proceedings and steps up to discovery, with further limitation or a full certificate sought by amendment request.
Quotes: "You will need to make an application to representation higher." | "Generally, the Agency will limit the certificate to certain steps in proceedings so as to minimise the exposure of the fund in the early stages of the case." | "Often certificates will initially be limited to investigation of the potential claim under the pre-action protocol, including obtaining the assisted person’s medical records and consideration thereof." | "As the matter progresses, the next limitation is likely to be the issuing of proceedings, replies and steps up to obtaining discovery."
Links: LAMS Supplier Manual -> https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/publications/lams-supplier-manual; Instructional Videos -> https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/lams-instructional-videos

says.detail:
The Limitation (Northern Ireland) Order 1989 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisi/1989/1339/article/7)
The legislation sets a time limit of three years for personal injury negligence claims: “that period is three years from— (a) the date on which the cause of action accrued, or (b) the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.” The date of knowledge is when the person first had knowledge that the injury was significant, attributable to the negligence, nuisance or breach of duty, and of the defendant’s identity (and, if relevant, the other person’s identity and supporting facts).
Quotes: "Except where paragraph (5) applies, that period is three years from—" | "(a) the date on which the cause of action accrued, or" | "(b) the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured." | "references to a person's date of knowledge are references to the date on which he first had knowledge of the following facts—"

says.detail:
The Conditional Fee Agreements Order 2013 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2013/9780111533437/note?view=plain)
The note says that article 4 specifies personal injury claims, and that in a claim for personal injuries the success fee is capped at 25% of specified damages. It also says this cap applies only at first instance; for appeals, the maximum success fee is 100% of those damages.
Quotes: "Article 4 specifies claims for personal injury for these purposes." | "Article 5 provides that, in a claim for personal injuries, the success fee shall be limited to a maximum of 25% of the damages awarded for pain, suffering and loss of amenity and pecuniary loss, other than future pecuniary loss and net of any sums recoverable by the Compensation Recovery Unit, inclusive of VAT." | "Article 5 further limits the effect of the 25% cap to proceedings at first instance." | "In respect of all other personal injury proceedings (i.e. appeals), the maximum success fee which may be recovered from damages awarded for pain, suffering and loss of amenity and pecuniary loss, other than future pecuniary loss and net of any sums recoverable by the Compensation Recovery Unit, shall be a maximum of 100% of those damages, inclusive of VAT."

trace.detail:
Question: For clinical negligence claims in Northern Ireland, what does this page say about when legal aid is available, for adults, and any key limits or tests? Quote the exact wording.
The page says legal aid for a clinical negligence claim is applied for through "representation higher," and that the certificate is generally limited in stages rather than given as a full certificate at the outset. It does not mention any special rule for adults or any means/merits test on this page. The key limit described is that the certificate is often initially restricted to investigation and pre-action steps, then later to issuing proceedings and steps up to discovery, with further limitation or a full certificate sought by amendment request.

✓ quote found in the page: "As the matter progresses, the next limitation is likely to be the issuing of proceedings, replies and steps up to obtaining discovery."
